controls.title: Exterior lock hardware grade
controls.objective: Exterior and restricted-area doors use commercial-grade locks in working order.

evidence.description: Photo of each substandard or failed lock

questions.text: Are exterior and restricted-area doors fitted with ANSI/BHMA Grade 1 (or equivalent) locksets or exit devices in working order?
questions.guidance: Check markings on the lock or the hardware schedule. Partial: Grade 2 found on some doors. Photograph residential-grade hardware.

questions.text: Number of exterior or restricted-area doors that fail to latch and lock when closed by their own closer
questions.guidance: Let each door close from fully open and check it latches.

controls.title: Key control
controls.objective: Keys are registered, issued on authorization, recovered at separation, and master keys use a restricted keyway.

questions.text: Is there a current key register listing each issued key, its holder, and authorization date?
questions.guidance: Partial: register exists but not updated in the last 12 months.

questions.text: Number of issued master or grand master keys that cannot be accounted for
questions.guidance: Reconcile the register with holders. Any unaccounted master key normally triggers a rekey.

questions.text: Do master keys use a restricted or patented keyway that cannot be duplicated without authorization?
questions.guidance: Check the key marking or the locksmith's documentation.

controls.title: Door and frame hardening
controls.objective: Exterior door hinges, latches, and frames resist removal, shimming, and prying.

evidence.description: Photo of exposed hinge pins or unprotected latches

questions.text: Are out-swinging exterior doors fitted with non-removable hinge pins or security studs?
questions.guidance: Inspect from outside. Photograph exposed removable pins.

questions.text: Is each exterior latch protected by a latch guard, or is the door-to-frame gap at the latch 1/8 in (3 mm) or less?
questions.guidance: Measure the gap at the latch with a feeler gauge or ruler.

references.source: UFC 4-020-01, DoD Security Engineering Facilities Planning Manual
references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Accessible window security
controls.objective: Ground-floor and other accessible windows have working locks and are closed when unattended.

evidence.description: Photo of each unlocked or broken window lock

questions.text: Are all accessible windows fitted with working locks and found closed and locked when the room is unattended?
questions.guidance: Accessible means reachable from grade or a climbable feature. Partial: locks present but some found open.

references.source: UFC 4-020-01, DoD Security Engineering Facilities Planning Manual
references.note: paraphrase; source not checked from the build container

controls.title: Equipment rack and cabinet locks
controls.objective: Network racks and cabinets holding live equipment are locked and their keys are controlled.

evidence.description: Photo of each unlocked rack or cabinet

questions.text: Are network racks, patch cabinets, and wall-mounted enclosures with live equipment locked, with keys held by named people?
questions.guidance: Check every rack and closet visited. Partial: locked but keys left in the lock or unlabeled.

controls.title: Combination and code changes
controls.objective: Safe combinations and keypad codes are changed when a person who knows them leaves or a compromise is suspected.

questions.text: Were safe combinations and keypad codes changed after the most recent departure of a person who knew them?
questions.guidance: Compare the change log with recent departures. Partial: changed, but more than 30 days after departure.

questions.text: Months since keypad and safe codes were last changed
